steps.note: S4.1.6 states the net target change (JV+RG)x independent of the initial scratch values a,c because rows 0-1 subtract the old contribution, and S4.1.5 says the last two rows restore the scratch values, matching the paper.
S4.1.7 gives the bit-case central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, side injection cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, intersections zero or two already zero, and self coefficient one.
S4.1.8 gives the complex central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2, cancelled by the side wires for distinct triples with intersection zero or two, intersection one contributing zero, as in the paper.
S4.1.9 states the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) with every invocation restoring its own scratch wires.

The plan asserts that every edge joins comparable labels and its S4.3.4 method says to tabulate the residual of every edge, but it never gives the per-edge residual table (only the gate-label table in S4.3.4.1 and the single residuals of side 2->5 and center 3->4), so the table is named without its content.
S4.3.4.2 states t_X perp t_Y gives <t_X> inside t_Y^perp, nested labels, and residual P tensor <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2.
S4.3.4.3 makes center 3->4 the only decreasing edge, losing h, with L=Ich, and S4.3.4.4 telescopes through the gates to sources N, sinks Wm-N, signed Wm-2N, absolute sum plus 2L.

S4.3.4.5 states that over F_2 every nonzero residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating (it contains a coordinate unit of norm one), hence has an orthonormal basis; the plane-absorption argument is not spelled out, but the defining content is there.
S4.3.5 states L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2.
S4.3.7.3 derives additivity of weight mod 4 for orthogonal binary vectors and S4.3.7.4 gives q_V-q_U = sum over an orthonormal residual basis of wt(v)[v.x] mod 4 (negated on decreasing edges).
S4.3.7.4 notes wt(v) is odd, and S4.3.7.5 writes i^{eps[v.x]} as (1+i^eps)/2+(1-i^eps)/2 (-1)^{v.x} and uses H diag(1,-1) H = X to get the kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse.

The interface step itself stays single-column, but S4.6.1.4 states that on f columns each residual basis vector gives one tensored factor (C^{eps})^{tensor f}, and S4.6.1.7 (with S4.3.7.2) gives s_c such factors in all, which is the sub-step's content in the coordinate form the paper also uses.

S4.3.7.6 gives C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a) for X_a->Y_a, repaired by Z_{a,k} before and i^{27k}Z_{a,k} after via C=iZC^{-1}Z, and S4.3.7.7 negates the X outputs; the explicit remark that the zero label has frame I and the full label C^{tensor m} is not stated, but the endpoint mechanism is.
S4.3.5 says both loss ratios are below 1/2 so a strict saving remains, S4.3.6.2 gives s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m, and S4.3.7.2 gives s_c<W_c m with deficit 2N-2L_c>0.
S4.4.1 defines eta=(Wm-s)/(Wm) and gives eta_b=339/22587335000000.
The plan states both deficits exceed 20*2^-50, log m<20, m^{1-2^-50}=m exp(-2^-50 log m)>m(1-20*2^-50)>m(1-eta), hence s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^-50.

S4.5.1.2 describes the pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, clearing by lower-triangular elementary multiplications, deleting the pivot row and column and repeating, and S4.5.1.1 gives Pi with exactly a ones.
S4.5.1.3 states a fixed odd prime avoiding all denominators and diagonal numerators in a finite table of factors, so the identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors.
S4.5.1.4 states a lower-triangular transformation of H or D costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order.
S4.5.1.5 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, an interchange, D_j<-H_i-D_j, yielding (h+d,d) with one interchange per one of Pi, a in all.
S4.6.4.1-2 give E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu, C_1=max{20,nu+3}, C_0=128mB^2, Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}), with nu=11 and C_1=20 for the complex network.
S4.6.4.5 states A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E at an internal node and A(e)<=8e at a leaf, and S4.6.4.3-4 derive the per-invocation count 24W^3+4s+4W+4 below E.
S4.6.4.6 unrolls with sx+E<=Bx and B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu to A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1}, and S4.6.4.7 bounds the total below 128mB^2 d^{nu+3}<=C_0 d^{C_1}.
S4.6.4.8 puts depth-l values in 2^{-(p+l)}Z[i] with modulus at most 2^l, so p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits are exact, and S4.6.4.9 uses epsilon C_1<1 to get Delta=o(p).
S4.6.5.6 states every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved, and truncation errs by less than sqrt2 2^-p.

summary: P03 states 25 of the 26 sub-steps, mostly as dedicated infer steps quoting the paper's own lines: all of bank-exchange (4/4), complex-phase-interface (4/4), rank-saving (4/4), matrix-shear (4/4) and simultaneous-layer (5/5), and 4/5 of label-residual-budget. The one absent sub-step is L1: the per-edge residual table is named in a method but never given (only the gate-label table and two individual residuals appear). Two credits are worth flagging: P3 is stated in the butterfly-layer steps (S4.6.1.4, S4.6.1.7), not in the interface proof, and P4 omits the explicit zero-label/full-label frames I and C^{tensor m}. Nothing is stated contrary to the paper.
